creature_families: UFO set: floating family, 6 rows, floatHeight set (units.rul 311-431)
UFO set: heavy armoured family, 3 rows (units.rul 619-665)
UFO set: single-row living weapons: robotic disc (283), reaper (455), chryssalid (595), silacoid (688), celatid (714), sectopod (809), zombie (834)

TFTD set (xcom2): aquatoid 6 rows (from units.rul:2), gillman 4, tasoth 2, lobsterman 5 (from 266), deep one 1, triscene 1 (409), xarquid 1, calcinite 1, tentaculat 1 (484), hallucinoid 1, biodrone 1 (535), zombie 1
Each family is a ladder of roles; rank index chosen per deployment (alienDeployments.rul)

Escalation: race weights by months (alienMissions.rul:6, RuleMissionScript.cpp:321-326); item tier by month (alienItemLevels.rul:2, BattlescapeGenerator.cpp:1098); quantity by difficulty band plus RNG(0,dQty) (BattlescapeGenerator.cpp:1081-1089); outside-craft chance (BattlescapeGenerator.cpp:1093)

top_creatures.label: Hive-walker
top_creatures.why: Highest front armour of any creature row in the UFO set (armors.rul:243); a walking chassis that reads at 375 wide.
top_creatures.keep: Heavy front, weaker rear and underside, so the flank matters.
top_creatures.change: The plate that breaks off becomes a visible break; not a generic walker shell.

top_creatures.label: Bone-blade runner
top_creatures.why: Melee only (firing skill zero), the largest time-unit pool of any UFO-set creature row (units.rul:595), and an infection chain: a zombie hit makes the victim rise as a zombie, and a zombie on death becomes this runner (units.rul:856; MeleeAttackBState.cpp:244-245; UnitDieBState.cpp:230).
top_creatures.keep: A fast melee-only body and a one-step infection that shows on the victim.
top_creatures.change: The infection has a visible timer and can be cured; the second form is ours, not a copy.

top_creatures.label: Floating ladder
top_creatures.why: Six-role family of hovering units, one readable ladder from soldier to commander, same hover height across the family.
top_creatures.keep: One family, six roles; rank raises stats and armour.
top_creatures.change: Each role gets its own silhouette, not one body with a palette swap.

top_creatures.label: Heavy brute
top_creatures.why: High-health body with three armour tiers by rank; reads well at distance.
top_creatures.keep: A tanky body with tiered armour per role.
top_creatures.change: Armour plates are separate sprite layers that can be lost mid-fight.

top_creatures.label: Mech dome
top_creatures.why: A living weapon that explodes on death (specab 1, src/Mod/Unit.h:26); the player knows what a kill costs.
top_creatures.change: The death is a shock ring with a short warning, not a blast.
top_creatures.ref: xcom1/units.rul:283 (row and specab at 308); src/Mod/Unit.h:26; src/Battlescape/BattlescapeGame.cpp:542

top_creatures.label: Acid spitter
top_creatures.why: Highest firing skill of any UFO-set creature row; built-in acid firearm row (items.rul CELATID_WEAPON, damage type 8).
top_creatures.keep: Ranged acid as its own damage type.
top_creatures.change: Acid leaves a pool on the floor the player can walk around.

top_creatures.label: Walking mother
top_creatures.why: The body leaves a second body on death (zombieUnit field); the usual kill becomes the start of a second fight.
top_creatures.keep: A death that spawns a follow-up.
top_creatures.change: The follow-up is a different creature from the zombie, with its own silhouette.

top_creatures.label: Burning spore pod
top_creatures.why: Burns the floor and explodes on death (specab 3, src/Mod/Unit.h:26); fire and blast in one death.
top_creatures.change: Fire stays on the tile where it dies; the warning is a glow on the ground before the blast.

classes: Human soldier: one type (xcom2/soldiers.rul:2) with a rank ladder; sergeant to commander add value bonuses 1, 3, 6, 10 (src/Savegame/BattleUnit.cpp:113-116)
UFO-set alien lists: 6 (xcom1/alienRaces.rul), including a five-family mixed list (line 52)
TFTD-set alien lists: 12 (xcom2/alienRaces.rul from line 2), including underwater variants and mixed crews (line 90)
Rank index picks the role inside a list; commander first in each list (alienRaces.rul:4)
Progression shape: stronger families and stronger item tiers appear with months passed (alienMissions.rul, alienItemLevels.rul)
weapon_families: UFO plasma ladder: pistol, rifle, heavy (xcom1/items.rul:762, 722, 682), clips of damage type 5
UFO laser ladder: pistol, rifle, heavy (damage type 4)
UFO projectile ladder: pistol, rifle, heavy cannon, auto cannon, with AP, HE and incendiary ammo rows (damage types 1, 3, 2)
UFO rocket family: launcher with small, large and incendiary rockets (damage types 3 and 2)
TFTD gauss ladder: pistol (xcom2/items.rul:527), rifle (565), heavy (604); clips of damage type 4
TFTD torpedo swap: one launcher (447) with small (470), large (489), phosphorous (508) ammo rows
TFTD sonic family and thermal shok (978, 1001; damageType 6 at 1013 = stun)
Living weapons: creature bodies as weapons (melee type 7), no item
Special properties: 10 damage types (src/Mod/RuleItem.h:27); smoke converts to stun before damage (src/Savegame/BattleUnit.cpp:1108)
gear_tiers: Human tiers, 4 per set: none, light (personal armour / plastic aqua), heavy (power suit / ion), top (flying suit / magnetic ion) (xcom1/armors.rul:54; xcom2/armors.rul:84)
Armour rows carry four facing values (front, side, rear, under) and a 10-entry damage multiplier list (armors.rul)
Facing picked from the hit vector (src/Savegame/BattleUnit.cpp:1096-1178); armour wears by power/10 + 1 per hit (BattleUnit.cpp:1213)
Creature hide rows: 12 families per set; lobsterman tiers 0 to 2 rise with rank (xcom2/armors.rul:241)
Tier shown by sprite sheet (spriteSheet field) plus inventory sprite (spriteInv); layer order from drawingRoutine (src/Battlescape/UnitSprite.cpp)
zones: UFO set: 10 terrains (xcom1/terrains.rul:2 onward): farmland, desert, forest, jungle, mars, mountain, polar, underground base, urban, alien base
TFTD set: 22 terrains (xcom2/terrains.rul:2 onward): seabed, pipes, plane site, sunken and ruined sites, volcano, coral reef, port, island, cargo site, alien bases, level set, crypt
Dungeon-like archetype: alien base carves tunnels with digTunnel and swaps wall and floor tiles (xcom1/mapScripts.rul:74, 88)
Boss archetype: BOSSBATTLE map script (xcom1/mapScripts.rul:105) and Cydonia landing and final assault deployments (alienDeployments.rul:1168, 1246)
Mission-as-zone: terror (alienDeployments.rul:706), alien base assault (843), base defence (body not read)
Hazards: debris map sets (seabed); day or night as a shade value per deployment; always-day and always-night utility rulesets (bin/standard/XcomUtil_Always_Daytime, XcomUtil_Always_Nighttime)

looks.label: Breathing bubbles (idle)
looks.technique: Armour row flag drawBubbles starts a breath frame; overlay drawn from the breath sheet with an offset for kneeling or short units.

looks.label: Fire overlay
looks.technique: A burning unit draws a frame from the smoke sheet, advancing with animation frame.

looks.label: Per-unit recolour
looks.technique: Colour-replace shader recolours a unit layer at draw time; one sprite, many colour sets.

looks.label: Shade per deployment
looks.technique: Shade value per deployment sets the map light; utility rulesets force day or night.

looks.label: Corpse variants
looks.technique: Four corpse rows per big unit type; death pose from data, one of four.
looks.ref: xcom1/items.rul (REAPER_CORPSE_1 to 4, SECTOPOD_CORPSE_1 to 4, CYBERDISC_CORPSE_1 to 4)

looks.label: Projectile strips per environment
looks.technique: Land and underwater projectile strips of the same size; the set changes with the environment.
looks.ref: xcom2 bullet sheets (TFTD-LAND, TFTD-UNDERWATER); xcom1 BulletSprites (per AU041, not re-read here)

looks.label: Screen filters
looks.technique: 24 GLSL shader files as a menu of screen looks (scanline, CRT, bloom, pixel scalers); only public-domain ones are safe to read for ideas.

originals.name: Campaign Tide
originals.idea: Enemy mix as a step table keyed to the player's progression stage, not months.
originals.keep: Step-function weights and the highest-key-not-above rule (RuleMissionScript.cpp:321-326).
originals.change: Keyed to zone tier and progression, not a calendar. Defect to fix before use: the while loop at RuleMissionScript.cpp:326 has no end check; fix by sorting keys on load and clamping below the first key.

originals.name: Rot Chain
originals.idea: A melee hit marks the victim to rise, and the rising body becomes a second creature on its own death.
originals.change: A visible timer on the victim that a shrine can cancel; the second form is ours.

originals.name: Four-Facing Shell
originals.idea: Armour per facing; the hit side is chosen from the hit vector; armour loses durability each hit.
originals.keep: The 8-way side mapping, side subtraction and the durability loss (BattleUnit.cpp:1096-1213).
originals.change: Lost durability shows as a crack; no random edge flip in fast duels.

originals.name: Chain Guard
originals.idea: When an action happens, the best-scoring guard acts first; if it cannot, the next is tried.
originals.change: Each guard pays stamina; the result is server-verified.

originals.name: Stance Dial
originals.idea: A 0, 1, 2 aggression number changes odds and stance.
originals.keep: The three states and their odds multipliers (AIModule.cpp:1296-1310).
originals.change: Three named stances the player reads from the pose and a sound cue, not a hidden number.

originals.name: Living Edge
originals.idea: Creatures whose body is the weapon; melee only; no separate item to drop.
originals.keep: No item to drop (living-weapon rows, units.rul 283, 455, 595).
originals.change: The body silhouette is the weapon; the kill shows what the creature was.

originals.name: Burn Ground
originals.idea: A unit that burns the floor when it moves and explodes on death.
originals.keep: Fire that stays where it was walked (UnitWalkBState.cpp:181; Unit.h:26).
originals.change: The floor glow is a visible warning before the blast.

originals.name: Thermal Stun
originals.idea: A stun-type damage type that knocks out and never kills.
originals.keep: A separate stun pool (RuleItem.h:27; xcom2/items.rul:1001 and 1013).
originals.change: A visible shock ring from the fight camera.
